unite_adi: UPPER SECONDARY-PREP YEAR-LEVEL: B1 - THEME 9: SCHOOL LIFE & EDUCATION

bolumler.ogrenmeKanitlari: PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT: Students write and design a school drama play on the content of ''different types of schools in the world, extracurricular activities at school, dealing with school anxiety'' and then they present it and perform it as a show in class by inviting other students as actors, directors, etc. The assignment will be evaluated by using rubrics. Öğrenme-Öğretme Yaşantıları
bolumler.temelKabuller: This theme includes the concept of ''schools and school life with its components such as different types of schools in the world, extracurricular activities at school, dealing with school anxiety'' and it is assumed that it could be present in almost all languages, with some exceptions. It is assumed that a student in the preparatory year of an upper secondary school may know what different types of schools in the world, extracurricular activities at school, dealing with school anxiety mean in their own language as it is known that almost all people who start to learn a new language bring their pre-existing knowledge (in their own language) with them and transfer it to their new language learning context. However, they may not know how to say these things in another language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. Fortunately, this existing knowledge in their own language can help them recognise, understand, and learn them more easily in a foreign language, in this case English. As they are students in the preparatory year of an upper secondary school, they are expected to know some basic vocabulary about ''schools and school life'' in English from previous years such as ''school life, an assignment, a state school, education and so on'' and also some structures such as ''Don’t be late for class!, The caretaker keeps the school clean, You read silently in the library., I am responsible for arriving at school on time, Can I leave early today?'' in English from the previous themes and/or years. These grammar items and vocabulary are revised during the ''Revision Programme'' at the beginning of the year and they can be used as a basis for learning the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme, so that the new grammatical elements in the current theme can be learnt easily.
bolumler.onDegerlendirme: It is assumed that these students in the preparatory year of an upper secondary school are ready to learn the concept of ''different types of schools in the world, extracurricular activities at school, dealing with school anxiety'' cognitively, affectively, and socially since it is appropriate to their age and language level. Therefore, a contextual poster or a large picture could be provided for the students to remember and practise the items that they are related and previously learnt so that they can discuss the poster and/or the picture in pairs and write down what they remember. This session can help them revise all the related vocabulary and grammatical elements that they have already learnt from previous themes or from previous years as a preparatory practice. In this way, their performance can be evaluated in terms of how much they remember and how accurately they use these items to build their competence in the current theme. It can help the teacher decide what to emphasise, revise, and practise in order to facilitate the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme. (Their performance can be evaluated by rubrics, a rating scale, and /or a marking scheme during these practices.).
bolumler.zenginlestirme: Objective: To compare different types of schools and extracurricular activities around the world in English and to write a short paragraph about them by using the target vocabulary and the target grammar. Activity 1: School Type Profiles Students research two different types of schools, such as public schools and international schools, focusing on key aspects like teaching methods, extracurricular activities, and support systems. They write a single descriptive paragraph using the present passive voice to summarise their findings. For example: ''In some public schools, free lunches are provided to students to support their education, while in international schools, language immersion programs are provided to enhance multilingual proficiency''. Based on their research, students create an introduction poster with visuals and passive sentences, which they present to the class. After each presentation, the teacher provides constructive feedback on grammar, content, and presentation skills, ensuring a comprehensive learning experience. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity. Objective: To describe and talk about anxiety causes and solutions at school in English by using target vocabulary and target grammar. Activity 2: Mapping Anxiety and Solutions The teacher starts by hanging two large, blank posters on the classroom walls: one titled ''Causes of Anxiety'' and the other ''Solutions for Anxiety''. Students brainstorm and write their ideas on sticky notes, placing them on the appropriate posters. For example, a student might write ''Exam stress is caused by a lack of preparation'' for the ''Causes poster'' and ''Relaxation techniques are introduced to reduce stress'' for the ''Solutions poster''. If technology is available, students can use a web 2.0 tool to create a real-time word cloud that visualises the most common causes and solutions provided by the class. After analysing the posters or word cloud, students write a paragraph in the present passive voice summarising the ideas. For example: ''Relaxation techniques are introduced to reduce exam stress. Peer support groups are organised to help students share their feelings''. Finally, students present their summaries to the class, and the teacher provides constructive feedback on grammar (passive voice usage), content, and presentation skills. This activity combines creative collaboration with grammar practice and public speaking. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
bolumler.destekleme: Objective: To identify extracurricular activities at school around the world in English by using the target vocabulary. Activity 1: School Match-Up The teacher gives a worksheet featuring pictures of different school types and activities (e.g., a drama club, a football match, a boarding school). The worksheet includes a word bank (drama club, art class, music class). Students carefully look at the pictures and select the correct word from the Word Bank to write under each image (e.g., for a drama club picture, write ''drama club''). Once everyone completes the activity, the teacher points to each picture and asks questions such as, ''What is this?'' prompting students to answer, such as, ''This is a drama club''. The teacher focuses on correct pronunciation during the responses, providing positive feedback and encouragement for accurate answers. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity. Objective: To help students understand and identify the use of target vocabulary in context through using listening skills. Objective: To understand and identify different types of schools and extracurricular activities around the world in English by using the target vocabulary. Activity 2: Listen, Fill, and Perfect The teacher informs the students that they will listen to an audio recording and asks them to listen quietly and focus on understanding the overall meaning during the first listening. After this, the teacher distributes an information gap worksheet with blanks related to the audio. During the second listening, students work individually or in pairs to fill in the blanks based on what they hear. For the third listening, students check their answers, correct any errors, and complete any missing information. Once all students have completed the worksheet, they take turns reading their answers aloud to the class. The teacher provides feedback on pronunciation, accuracy, and overall language use. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
